_about: Memory matrix of image-model experiments for kids' webtoon strips. One entry per preset in data/styles.json. Qualitative notes from reviewing every panel by eye; numbers (renders, rerolls, speed) are computed from kids/runs/jobs.jsonl by kids/tools/matrix.py. Verdict scale: A = use as default, B = good with known fixes, C = only for specific shots, D = avoid.
lessons: Multi-character scenes (2–4 characters + animals) are where models differ most; single portraits are easy for all.
FLUX draws speech bubbles with gibberish when scene_en contains a verb of speaking (whispers, says, asks) — describe what is seen, not what is said; schnell does it far more often than dev.
SDXL (CLIP, ~77 tokens): character descriptions after the scene get merged into whoever the scene names first; put who first (who_first).
Booru anime checkpoints leak animal features onto humans (rabbit/fox/cat ears and tails) when an animal is in the same panel; negate 'animal ears, kemonomimi, fox tail' per panel.
Pony family draws animals as anthro characters unless tagged 'feral, quadruped' with 'anthro, humanoid, standing on two legs' negated.
Establishing/wide shots with SDXL drop the characters or the giant; a medium shot with the creature tags weighted brings them back.
A style word that is also an object gets drawn literally: Animagine 'storybook' put books in hands.
Realistic checkpoints (RealVis, CyberRealistic, Juggernaut Lightning) ignore drawn styles; claymation only took with weights (1.3–1.4) and a 'miniature diorama' framing.
FLUX-dev takes some media from the prompt alone (paper cut-out collage, chalk pastel, ink graphic novel, toy diorama with LoRA) but not others (pixel art, stained glass, two-tone risograph).
Same style on FLUX dev vs schnell is not always dev > schnell: schnell took linocut better (sharper carved lines) but signs/letters the image more often.

clean_webtoon.good: consistent cute characters, pastel, fast (~14 s)
clean_webtoon.bad: close-ups of animals turn abstract; duplicates a second character; fox kit's ears leak to the girl
clean_webtoon.fixes: negative_extra for duplicates and animal ears; medium shot instead of close-up for animals

illustrious_storybook.good: the most 'book-like' look, soft and consistent
illustrious_storybook.bad: duplicate rabbits; gardener drawn as a child; ice giant missing in wide shots; black-ear weight leaked onto a hat
illustrious_storybook.fixes: weight the creature in a medium shot; '(old man:1.3)'; avoid strong attribute weights

animagine_storybook.good: best night, lanterns and moonlight among SDXL
animagine_storybook.bad: 'storybook' → books in hands (fixed); swaps hair colours between two kids; lost the chihuahua and the acrobat once
animagine_storybook.fixes: aesthetic 'illustration, painterly' and negate books; medium shots for small animals

animagine_nouveau.bad: test panel lost the fox and the action (cotton candy instead of notebook)

hassaku_storybook.bad: put bunny ears on the girl in the first test

illustrious_pixar.bad: chaotic tiny characters underwater, empty classroom instead of ghost + cat

noobai_flat.good: strong, clean graphic look; overgrown ruins look great
noobai_flat.bad: rabbit ears on the girl, extra rabbits
noobai_flat.fixes: negate animal ears / multiple rabbits per panel

juggernaut_pixar.bad: merges two characters (pug wears the girl's dress); third character never appears
juggernaut_pixar.fixes: who_first; best of 3; keep to one subject per panel

juggernaut_book.good: two subjects slightly better than with LoRA
juggernaut_book.bad: still bleeds clothes onto the dog

pony_pixar.bad: never drew the pumpkin king next to the girl; kitten turned into a masked girl/raccoon
pony_pixar.fixes: feral/quadruped + anti-anthro; creature only in solo shots

atomix_space.good: excellent humans (Viktorie, captain); LoRA shows in backgrounds
atomix_space.fixes: feral, quadruped; negate anthro, humanoid, cat ears

flux_pixar.good: holds 3–4 characters incl. animals; no fixes needed

flux_manga.good: zero fixes in two stories; ghost, owl, clock, shark, mermaid all right

flux_toybox.good: the most consistent characters of all; tilt-shift toy look

flux_schnell_ink.good: ~2× faster than dev, style as good
flux_schnell_ink.bad: draws speech bubbles / watermarks (4 of 26 panels)
flux_schnell_ink.fixes: scene_en without speech verbs; extra_en 'Absolutely no speech bubbles, no lettering'

flux_dev_pixel.bad: pixel art not taken — plain cartoon
flux_dev_pixel.fixes: a pixel-art LoRA would be needed

flux_papercut.good: style clearly taken from the prompt alone

flux_chalk.good: soft texture, ghost + cat right on first try

flux_stainedglass.bad: no stained glass look; fox tail behind the girl

realvis_matte.bad: ignores painted styles; wrong dog breed once
realvis_matte.fixes: describe the breed in scene_en, negate wrong breeds

cyberreal_clay.good: plasticine figures with fingerprints once weighted
cyberreal_clay.bad: drifts back to photo (a real-looking girl), a herd instead of one goat

flux_gouache.good: girl, fawn, cat and pies right on the test panel
flux_gouache.bad: hen missing, her straw hat landed on the fawn

flux_felt.good: style fully taken; octopus and ghost-in-portrait both right

flux_vintage.good: acrobat + chihuahua in red jacket right

flux_folk.bad: ice giant missing; fox tail leaked onto the girl

flux_linocut.bad: cat drawn as a spotted deer-dog

flux_schnell_linocut.good: took linocut better than dev did

animagine_ukiyoe.bad: tiny girl next to a giant fox, the ice giant missing

noobai_chibi.bad: empty purple scene, the shark and octopus missing
